verdict.rationale: Decagon documents mechanisms for scoped, minimal-privilege agent access (short-lived JWTs discarded per session, IdP-based access via Okta/Entra) and shows agents can act inside connected systems via Browser Actions/integrations, which supports the general claim of taking real actions with scoped auth. However, no concrete evidence names specific business actions like refunds, order changes, or subscription updates, nor shows per-action (vs per-session) authorization granularity. Missing for 10: explicit examples of refund/order/subscription action execution, per-action (not just per-session) scoping detail, and independent/hands-on verification of these action flows.
